purpose: Compare ordinary and Common Work Core-assisted agents on a realistic Android game project workflow.

sourceContextAudit.reason: The source thread already contained a highly structured assistant-authored launch plan, so full-history access would measure retrieval and summarization rather than autonomous planning.
sourceContextAudit.roughTrialInput: Six user-authored planning messages plus two current-state facts; prior assistant plans excluded. Verbatim source text is intentionally not stored in this shareable artifact.

design.difference: The harness arm received the exact Common Work Core after the same curated brief.
design.limitation: The curated brief itself included scope, assumption, verification, and claim-integrity guidance, reducing treatment separation.

trials.verdict: Small reliability and handoff improvement, but weak evidence of incremental value because the control brief already encoded several harness behaviors.

design.difference: Both arms received the same rough user-memory packet and no prior assistant plan; only the harness arm received the Common Work Core.
design.allowedActions: Read-only planning and current official web research; no implementation or file modification.

observedStrengths: Autonomously completed a launch-oriented plan without unnecessary questions.
Produced a concise MVP, verification criteria, release sequence, and developer handoff.
observedRisks: Committed early to session length, a two-second loss threshold, a visual theme, and a minimum Android version without clearly routing those decisions back to the user.

observedStrengths: Separated unknown account conditions from confirmed facts.
Covered offline recovery, score resubmission, signing, release evidence, data disclosure, QA, and handoff concerns.
Completed the task without an approval loop or implementation overreach.
observedRisks: Expanded into Korean and English support, music, detailed game rules, package naming, device counts, and a compressed schedule without enough evidence that all were required now.
The longer multi-pass workflow amplified the full-core context cost.

trials.verdict: The harness arm was more operationally responsible and handoff-ready, but its quality gain did not clearly justify the 29.63% total-token increase and broader scope.

provisionalConclusion.quality: Common Work Core V1 shows meaningful omission-risk reduction on rough planning input.
provisionalConclusion.efficiency: The full always-on core is not yet token-efficient for multi-pass planning work.
provisionalConclusion.decision: Keep V1 unchanged until design-planning, visual-design, and runnable-code stages are observed; then decide whether to retain the full core or split a compact always-on core from routed role modules.
provisionalConclusion.generalization: Not claimed; each trial is a single paired observation.
